Messages.Author: Brum
Messages.Body:
Very late Report, but I was completely swamped for the last couple of months.
Although for good reasons.
Besides, me being the winner, made this report go down a bit on the huge stack of things to do.

Portuguese National Championship 2012
Lisboa, Portugal
December 15th, 2012
12 Players
3R + F

Deck Name: Better Gents, Same Sticks, No Parity Shifts. Ever.
Author: Tiago Brum
Description: Govern Superior as much as possible.
Most times, people don't see this deck as the table threat, even after 4 minions.
I think it's because players have irrational fears of stealth, big cap vampires, players with vote lock, pure rush, walls...
I'm happy with list. Almost the same list that I took to the Final of EC 2012.

Created with Secret Library v0.9.4a. (Feb 22, 2013 13:36:41)

Final Table:

Me (Ventrue Grinder)
Eliseu Ângelo (Kyasid Stealth n Bleed)
Ricardo Marta (Girls Will Find aids)
José "Zedú" Rodrigues (Rachel Brandywine)
André Catarino (G4 IC Counsil of Doom)

Tried to sit in a place were people didn't block my Sup Governs.
Besides a kickass opening hand, in turn 4 or 5 my Predator made a small mistake and a huge mistake. Both in a row.
Lets just say he was left with no vampires and 21 pool.

I had Deflections and Delaying Tactics, but still it was a game changer.
By this time my Prey had 5 minions with dom, mit and obt and Ricardo was in trouble.
I Pentexed Rachel to protect my Pool Cushion of a Predator. Ricardo had to go backwards as much as he could, so Zedu would eventually get his VP.
Ricardo was ousted eventually, but so was my Prey, who had little to no blood in his vamps after ousting Ricardo and had to tap out to try to oust Zedu.
Before dying, my Prey made a Golconda on a recently freed Rachel. Zedu decided lots of pool was better than Rachel + Victoria.
Everybody thought 30 min was little time and maybe Zedu thought that 1 VP would be enough, being top seed.

The thing is - the game went suddently from 5 to 3 player and each turn around the table took much less time.
After ousting Eliseu it was innevitable to oust Zedu.
5 or 6 minions Vs Victoria and Gregor Anderssen.
Zedu kept playing fast, even when time would give him Victory. A gentleman.

It was a pleasure playing with these gentlemen, although my Predator's mistake took some fun out of it.
I also made at least one mistake by tapping everyone when I should've left one minion untapped to stop Victoria from breaking Rachel's Pentex.
I might've gotten one more VP in the Final.

Hope everybody had fun.
3 new people qualified for next EC and hope to go with me, so that's very cool too.

Cheers!
Tiago, NC^2 for Portugal

Messages.Author: Brum
Messages.Body:
> Ira wrote:
>
> > Brum wrote:
> > in turn 4 or 5 my Predator made a small mistake and a huge mistake. Both in a row.
> > Lets just say he was left with no vampires and 21 pool.
> >
> So what was the mistake, specifically?
>
He had 2 Inner Circles with 1 and 2 blood each.
Mistake #1: he did bigger Villeins than he needed.
Mistake #2: The one with 1 blood tried to hunt. His rationale was that I had used many 2nd Traditions already and wouldn't try to block this.
My rationale was that, worse case scenario, it would be nice to make him use blood, either by Elder Impersonation, Forgotten Labyrinth or Majesty. Blocked and torporized Rafael.
Mistake #3: Adana diablerizes Rafael. André is a competitive player for 2 to 3 years, who has been out of VtES for about 9 months.
Also, he was probably very tired.
We asked "Are you sure??? You know we're gonna toast Adana, right???"
"Yeah, I'm sure!". Later we said he thought Rafael could still vote...
On his own words - "If the game goes too well, or not well at all, I lose my concentration and do stupid mistakes".
He had another Rafael on the uncontrolled area, but me and his Predador voted for Rafael to toast.

So I ended up with 3 cards I couldn't cycle for a few turns, but it was obviously a good trade off.

Messages.Author: Brum
Messages.Body:
Sometimes players are less in control of the speed they play than one might think.
Looking at the footage of last EC's Final I still surprise myself how slow I played, because when I was there I thought I was playing normally fast.
It was totally involuntary.
The extra table talk was because I was nervous, being my first big Final and all. Maybe my slow speed was also because of that.

BTW, extra kudos to Zedú, because he's starting to become more and more experienced and isn't afraid to contact people much more experienced than him for tips on his favorite decks.

Many players see guys like Hugh, the Brothers, or other top players as inaccessible champions who deserve reverence and should be dealt with at a distance.
I've never met anyone in this game like that.

Messages.Author: Zédu
Messages.Body:
Hi all.

First thanks for the compliments Tiago, if I'm better its mostly your fault.

> Brum wrote:
> Before dying, my Prey made a Golconda on a recently freed Rachel. Zedu decided lots of pool was better than Rachel + Victoria.
> Everybody thought 30 min was little time and maybe Zedu thought that 1 VP would be enough, being top seed.
>
> The thing is - the game went suddently from 5 to 3 player and each turn around the table took much less time.
> After ousting Eliseu it was innevitable to oust Zedu.
> 5 or 6 minions Vs Victoria and Gregor Anderssen.
> Zedu kept playing fast, even when time would give him Victory. A gentleman.
>
this was the most difficult decision I had to make in this final, at the time Eliseu played the Golconda I already had Gregor whit PRO and about 4/6 pool, Eliseu had 5/6 Minions ready to bleed, my hand only had one 2ºtradition so my only possible choice was to gain the pool and try to survive until the time ended. In that turn I was left whit 4/6 pool again so if I didn't had given up Rachel and gained 10 pool Eliseu would have made my VP. I belive that playing the Golconda on Rachel was a mistake because of that.

This was my best Portuguese National Championship so far, I made my 1º objective that was to qualify for the EC. and almost made the ultimate objective that was to win the final. I really enjoyed playing that day.

I would like to say special thanks to Adam Esbjörnsson for the help and advice he gave me when preparing to this deck for this tournament.
